show_name: Furthest Reaches of Space (Ed Reads Short Sci-fi, vol. VIII)
show_description: Explore the cosmos with Wanderlust by Alan E. Nourse, where dreams clash with familial expectations before embarking on the ultimate journey. In The Sense of Wonder by Milton Lesser, a generational starship alters the very fabric of humanity as time stretches on. Mr Meek ‚Aì Musketeer! by Clifford D. Simak follows a mans retirement plans that spiral into moral dilemmas. Journey alongside the Wanderer of Infinity by Harl Vincent, where a science experiment opens a portal to uncharted worlds. In X Marks the Asteroid by Ross Rocklynne, a daring trip to Titan leads to family secrets and treacherous alliances. Blind Man‚As Lantern by Allen Kim Lang tells the story of an Amish couple navigating deep space to find their new home amidst other settlers in need. Travelogue by Roger Dee introduces us to a struggling sci-fi author who receives an enigmatic brochure that sparks his imagination. The Good Seed by Mack Reynolds reveals a crash landing on a distant planet, where a traveler faces life-altering revelations. Pen Pal by Milton Lesser takes us on a quest to uncover the story of a mysterious man found through local ads. Lastly, The Course of Logic by Lester del Rey challenges two deep space travelers with a bizarre new species that embodies the essence of humanity itself. Concluding with Journey for the Brave by Alan E. Nourse, we delve into the thoughts of the first man on the moon, revealing his inner fears and triumphs. - Summary by The Reader

show_description: The EUNIC London Podcast Series  EUNICAST: Meet Visionary Europeans is a brand new podcast series presenting some of Europe’s most talented and respected artists, performers and influencers expressing their opinions on the arts and current affairs and sharing their life stories and artistic influences.   A podcast series of EUNIC London (European National Institutes for Culture) presents seven episodes featuring in-depth interviews with leading European personalities from the field of arts, music, arts management and social sciences. In a discussion with award-winning BBC journalist Joe Lynam, they talk about the current situation and its impact on society in terms of their professional field and reflect on future developments.  Interviewees include: the Czech-British acclaimed journalist, TV presenter and former Director of the BBC Worlds Service and the Barbican Centre, Sir John Tusa; the Spanish ballet dancer and artistic director of the English National Ballet, Tamara Rojo; the German curator and historian of science and Director of the History of Science Museum at Oxford University, Silke Ackermann; the Estonian Grammy Award-winning conductor Paavo Järvi; the French lecturer in Modern and Contemporary Art and art collector Catherine Petitgas; the Austrian Director of the Academy of St Martin in the Fields Chamber Orchestra, Tomo Keller and the Lithuanian acclaimed artist, composer, musician and performer Lina Lapelyte.  The EUNIC London (European National Institutes for Culture) podcast series is prepared under the leadership of the Czech Centre London and in production collaboration with the Extraudionary.  The first two episodes will be released on the 8th of April 2021 via Spotify. Stay tuned!
